passages.original: Quapropter cum, sicut scripsistis, fratres dilectissimi, et ut Felix (64) et Sabinus collegae nostri asseverant, utque alius Felix de Caesarau- gusta32 (65) fidei cultor 1029 ac defensor veritatis litteris suis significat33, Basilides et Martialis nefan- do idololatriae libello contaminati sint, Basilides ad- huc insuper, praeter libelli maculam, cum in infir- mitate decumbereti, in Deum blasphemaverit et se blasphemasse confessus sit, et episcopatum pro conscientiae suae vulnere sponte deponens ad agen- dam poenitentiam conversus sit, 1030 Deum de- precans, et satis gratulans si sibi vel laico communi- care contingeret.
passages.english: Therefore, since, as you have written, dearest brothers, and as Felix and Sabinus our colleagues affirm, and as another Felix of Caesaraugusta, a cultivator of the faith and defender of the truth, indicates in his letter, Basilides and Martialis have been defiled by the abominable certificate of idolatry; [and since] Basilides moreover, besides the stain of the certificate, when he was lying in sickness, blasphemed against God and confessed that he had blasphemed, and, voluntarily laying down his episcopate because of the wound to his conscience, turned to doing penance, entreating God and counting himself fortunate enough if it should fall to him to communicate even as a layman.
passages.notes: The numerals (64), (65), 1029, 1030 and superscript marks (32, 33, and the stray 'i' in 'decumbereti') are editorial footnote and column markers, and have been omitted. 'Libellus' refers to the certificate of sacrifice obtained during the Decian persecution (hence 'libellatici'). The sentence is grammatically incomplete here; the main clause continues in the following passage.
